The men's ski cross event at the 2018 Winter Olympics took place at Phoenix Snow Park in Pyeongchang, South Korea. This event was one of the freestyle skiing disciplines featured in the Olympics.

### Date
The competition occurred on February 21, 2018.

### Format 
Ski cross is a race where four skiers compete head-to-head, navigating through a course with jumps, rollers, and high-banked turns. It's an elimination format, beginning with a seeding round to determine placements for the elimination rounds. Competitors then race in heats of four, with the top two from each heat advancing to subsequent rounds until the final determines the medalists.

### Results
The gold medal was won by Brady Leman from Canada. Leman's victory came after narrowly missing out on a medal at the Sochi 2014 Olympics, where he finished fourth. The silver medal went to Marc Bischofberger from Switzerland, while the bronze was won by Sergey Ridzik, representing the Olympic Athletes from Russia.

### Notable Incidents
The final of the men's ski cross was particularly dramatic. French skier Terence Tchiknavorian suffered a serious leg injury in the early rounds, causing significant delay and reshuffling in the heats. Additionally, another top contender, Kevin Drury of Canada, was involved in a crash in the big final but managed to finish, albeit out of the medal positions.

### Olympic Context
Ski cross was added to the Olympic program during the 2010 Winter Olympics in Vancouver, making the Pyeongchang games the third appearance of ski cross at the Olympics. The discipline has gained popularity for its excitement and the unpredictable nature of the races, highlighting high-speed action and tactical maneuvers.

The Men's Ski Cross in 2018 again demonstrated the thrilling and unpredictable nature of the sport, culminating in a dramatic final and showcasing the resilience and skill of top international competitors in freestyle skiing.
